findings.text: Claims C6 (closed appointments never change) and C7 (No-show definition) are declared, but no requirement cites their sources. REQ-6 cites only the ticket line, so these claims are not tied to any requirement.

rubric_items.reason: Each of the seven acceptance criteria maps to a requirement: AC2 is split into REQ-2 to REQ-5 and AC6 into REQ-9 to REQ-11. The user-story line is listed under Out of scope with a reason.
Each REQ covers one behaviour. REQ-3 and REQ-4 cannot yet be tested against an exact string because the date-time format is unknown (U-1, Q-01). The artifact says this openly.

The known items cite ticket lines or baseline sections. Asia/Kolkata comes from the baseline constraints, not from guesswork. REQ-13 is marked assumed, has a real basis in the glossary and baseline, and has a matching question (Q-04).

I found no clash between the ticket and the baseline. The ticket's 'hospital time zone' and 'no medical history' match the baseline constraints and data-protection rules, and the artifact cites both sides.
All questions are non-blocking with sensible defaults and real options. Format and policy questions go to the product owner; the appointment page and glossary questions go to the tech lead.
Plain wording. Glossary terms (Scheduled, No-show, Inactive, Medical history) are used consistently. Missing terms are listed with found: false.
